finding: src/anomaly/state.py:39 A completed snapshot with missing authoritative identities is trusted as P7-complete.
rationale: Normal sealing captures identities, but the public portable-case entry accepts any regular state.json; load_snapshot converts a missing or non-mapping identities value to {}, changed_identities cannot notice omitted required keys, and resolve_workflow then treats a sequential completed map through P7 as terminal and even projects README completion without validating the authoritative artifacts.

evidence.output: _seal_success normally calls capture_identities before write_state, but load_snapshot passes {} when identities is absent or malformed, and changed_identities compares only recorded.items(); it has no required-key check, so omitted identities produce no invalidation.

run_workflow is a real public entry: its case-tree guard rejects links/special files but accepts regular files, resume_case validates the case record rather than state provenance, then load_snapshot feeds resolve_workflow; resolve_workflow returns complete solely when completed_phase is P7.

completed_phase accepts any sequential P0-P7 key mapping; load_snapshot calls project_readme when it sees P7, and project_readme marks Status complete and adds accepted-findings/report links without checking that those artifacts or their identities exist.
